records.title: Outer Membrane Vesicles Derived From Klebsiella pneumoniae Aggravate Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis in Mdr2-/- Mice and IL-17A-Stimulated Cholangiocyte Organoids.
records.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a rare cholestatic liver disease characterized by chronic inflammation and biliary stricture; however, its pathogenesis remains poorly understood. PSC patients frequently have coexisting inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), accompanied by a pronounced enrichment of Klebsiella pneumoniae in the gut. Given the crucial role of bacterial outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) in disease pathogenesis, we hypothesize that K. pneumoniae-derived OMVs (Kp-OMVs) serve as key mediators between the gut and liver in PSC. In Mdr2-/- mice, Kp-OMVs exacerbated PSC, with increased cholestatic liver injury, fibrosis, and bile duct hyperplasia. Hepatic transcriptomics revealed significant activation of multiple pro-inflammatory pathways, along with marked suppression of glutathione metabolism, detoxification, and bile secretion. Moreover, Kp-OMVs disrupted the intestinal barrier, promoted endotoxin translocation, and disturbed the gut-liver microecology in Mdr2-/- mice. Notably, this was accompanied by increased hepatic abundances of Fusobacterium, Pseudomonas, and Campylobacter, as well as decreased abundances of Bifidobacterium and Muribaculaceae. However, in antibiotic-pretreated Mdr2-/- mice, Kp-OMVs aggravated hepatic inflammation and fibrosis but failed to induce intestinal barrier disruption. In vitro, treatment with Kp-OMVs further enhanced inflammation, induced senescence, and suppressed proliferation in IL-17A-stimulated cholangiocyte organoids, whereas Escherichia coli-derived OMVs (Ec-OMVs) did not elicit these effects. Mechanistically, Kp-OMVs upregulated the NF-kappa B, TNF, cytokine-cytokine receptor, and IL-17 signalling pathways in organoids. In conclusion, Kp-OMVs aggravate PSC via gut-liver axis disruption and activation of inflammatory signalling pathways, offering a potential therapeutic target for future intervention in PSC.

records.title: A simple prestaining protocol to enhance visualization and embedding of 3D breast cancer organoids for downstream histological analysis.
records.abstract: Three-dimensional patient-derived organoids (PDOs) from tumor tissue are more realistic in-vitro models than traditional two-dimensional cultures, preserving key features of primary tumors. However, processing organoids for histology is challenging: their small size, transparency, and dispersion in matrix gels make them difficult to locate during formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) processing, risking sample loss. To address this, we developed a simple, affordable prestaining method using reversible dyes-crystal violet, eosin-methylene blue (EMB), and neutral red-to visualize and track spheroids and PDOs before embedding. We first tested the staining, fixation, embedding, and destaining steps with MDA-MB-231 cell line spheroids, then applied the protocol to breast cancer PDOs. Pre-stained 3D structures remained visible during embedding and sectioning, and residual dye was removed by brief ethanol washes without affecting shape. Immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence for Ki67/phospho-ERK and CD49f/H3K27ac markers respectively confirmed that prestaining did not impair antigen detection. This protocol improves embedding accuracy, reduces sample loss, and preserves compatibility with further histological and immunohistochemical analysis, offering a practical way to process small 3D organoid samples.

records.title: Targeting SEC23A: Artesunate's dual pathway approach to reversing gastric metaplasia.
records.abstract: Artesunate (ART) is a promising multi-target drug, yet its efficacy and mechanism against intestinal metaplasia (IM)/spasmolytic polypeptide-expressing metaplasia (SPEM), a key precancerous gastric lesion with no effective therapy, remain unexplored. This work presented that ART reversed SPEM and IM progression in mice, selectively impairing IM cell viability via inducing paraptosis. Mechanistically, ART triggered paraptosis through dual pathways, involving reactive oxygen species (ROS)-dependent c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK)/P38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) activation and ROS-independent endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress via direct SEC23 homolog A (SEC23A) binding. ART disrupted SEC23A-SEC24 homolog A (SEC24A) dimer formation, inducing ER stress via promoting K63-linked ubiquitination and P62-mediated autophagic degradation of SEC23A. Moreover, its efficacy was confirmed in human-derived IM organoids, showing reduced growth, SEC23A degradation, and MAPK/ER stress activation. Taken together, ART alleviates gastric precancerous lesions by selectively inducing paraptosis through ROS-dependent JNK/P38 MAPK activation and SEC23A-targeted ER stress via coatomer protein complex II (COPII) disruption and autophagic degradation.

records.title: The RNA and protein landscapes of mouse brain organoids.
records.abstract: Organoids are powerful models of brain development and function. Mouse brain organoids reproduce the main steps of neurodevelopment in vivo and differentiate more rapidly than human organoids, making them scalable for screening applications. However, mouse brain organoids remain poorly defined. Here, we showed that the transcriptome and proteome of mouse brain organoids developed for three weeks are close to those of a neonatal mouse brain. Strikingly, organoids recapitulated the majority of alternative splicing and polyadenylation-site events that define neural identity in vivo. Proteomics revealed that most changes in mRNA expression were translated into proteins. Mouse brain organoids differentiated for only three weeks already harbored a complex network of synaptic proteins, including the ionotropic and metabotropic receptors for the neurotransmitters glutamate and GABA. To conclude, our study provides evidence that mouse brain organoids are a rapidly maturing and relevant model of mammalian brain development and function in a neonatal-like environment.

records.title: A benchmarking framework for organoid computing.
records.abstract: Organoid computing leverages functional neural networks of lab-grown neural organoids to recapitulate key aspects of human brain information processing, holding promising potential in brain-inspired computing, brain-computer interfaces, neuroscience, and medicine. However, its broad application remains constrained due to technical limitations including biological variability, interface instability, stochastic performance, and limited reproducibility. Here, we present a benchmarking framework that systematically quantifies the key performance determinants of organoid computing. We operationally define 'benchmark-ready' organoid substrates using optional criteria encompassing viability, cellular identity, structural integrity, functional maturation, and baseline networks, supported by multimodal phenotyping. We further establish qualification metrics for organoid-machine interface and intrinsic neural and network function, including physical coupling, spatial coverage, temporal stability, spontaneous activity, and network-level organization. Finally, we introduce a hierarchical evaluation framework for stimulation-evoked computation combined with information encoding criteria, standardized scoring, and statistical reporting. We believe that the benchmarking framework may provide an adaptable foundation for standardized, reproducible and comparable evaluation of organoid computing technologies, thereby facilitating the broad adoption and application of organoid intelligence.

records.title: Co-conditioning and parallel cell homing-driven pre-metastatic niche engineering: TGF-β-fuelled 3D microphysiological model for epithelial-mesenchymal transition in breast cancer.
records.abstract: Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells, also known as BMSCs, have been demonstrated to promote epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) cells, which contributes to the invasive and metastatic features of these cells. To be more specific, exosomes generated from bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSC) that include microRNAs like miR-210-3p have the ability to activate the Wnt/β-catenin pathway, which further promotes the advancement of TNBC. Factors like as TGF-β and HGF are included in the BMSC secretome, which is a collection of chemicals that are released. These factors have the potential to contribute to extracellular matrix (ECM) and other aggressive behaviours like TNBC. Variable 2D and 3D models have been explored over the years to generate stable phenotyping characteristics of EMT in triple-negative breast cancer. Within the scope of this review, we have provided an in-depth analysis of the pathophysiology of EMT in breast cancer, as well as the varied crosstalk that occurs between distinct signalling pathways. A variety of in vivo and patient-derived xenograft models have been reviewed, along with their respective applications and possible limitations. This article provides a comprehensive discussion on the several cutting-edge 3D microphysiological disease models (Organoid, Spheroid, and Organ-on-Chip) that facilitate the replication of the pathophysiology of EMT in breast cancer. We have critically discussed our experimental observation on BMSC mediated co-conditioning and parallel cell homing with MDA-MB-231 to induce stable EMT. It will act as a marker pathway for medication targeting, treatments, and emphasis on drug resistance as a 3D in vitro microphysiological disease model.

records.title: FeDx-SF@βE assembly for AML treatment via GATA1/SLC40A1 pathway-mediated iron homeostasis disorder.
records.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is an aggressive hematologic malignancy characterized by rapid progression, therapeutic resistance, and poor prognosis. Inducing ferroptosis in AML cells represents a promising therapeutic strategy. In this study, transcriptomic analyses first revealed that ferroptosis-associated transcriptional states were closely associated with prognosis and ex vivo drug-response heterogeneity in AML, providing a rationale for ferroptosis-oriented therapeutic design. Based on these findings, and further supported by a transcriptome-based target-scoring strategy, β-elemene (βE), a clinically used natural compound derived from traditional Chinese medicine, was selected as a candidate ferroptosis-related agent. We subsequently developed a nanodelivery system, designated FeDx-SF@βE, based on alcohol-induced silk fibroin (SF) folding to co-deliver ferric dextran (FeDx) and βE. The resulting nanoparticles exhibited a uniform particle size of 182.3 nm, favorable colloidal stability, and sustained drug release behavior. In vitro studies demonstrated efficient cellular uptake of FeDx-SF@βE by AML cells, leading to significantly inhibited cell viability. Pharmacological cell-death inhibitor rescue experiments showed that ferrostatin-1 produced the most pronounced protective effect, indicating that FeDx-SF@βE-induced AML cell death was predominantly ferroptosis-dependent. Mechanistically, βE-containing treatment suppressed the nuclear translocation of the transcription factor GATA1 and downregulated the iron efflux channel SLC40A1. GATA1/SLC40A1 gain- and loss-of-function analyses further demonstrated that activation of this axis attenuated FeDx-SF@βE-induced iron overload and ferroptotic injury, whereas suppression of this axis promoted intracellular iron retention, oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation, and mitochondrial damage. In combination with FeDx-derived iron supply, βE-mediated inhibition of the GATA1/SLC40A1 iron-export axis resulted in intracellular iron overload, glutathione depletion, ROS accumulation, extensive lipid peroxidation, and ferroptosis. Bulk transcriptomic and virtual-cell analyses further supported the involvement of the GATA1/SLC40A1 axis in ferroptosis-associated AML states and linked βE-related transcriptional programs to this regulatory mechanism. In a disseminated AML xenograft model, FeDx-SF@βE exhibited enhanced antileukemic efficacy and favorable biosafety. Collectively, this work provides a combined ferroptosis-oriented nanotherapeutic strategy for AML treatment and highlights the GATA1/SLC40A1 iron-homeostasis axis as a functionally relevant mechanism for ferroptosis-targeted nanomedicine design.

records.title: scREFINE: Label-efficient refinement of frozen scGPT embeddings for single-cell RNA-seq clustering.
records.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) clustering remains challenging because of high dimensionality, sparsity, technical noise, and limited cell annotations. Here, we propose scREFINE, a label-efficient semi-supervised clustering framework that adapts pretrained single-cell foundation-model embeddings for accurate cell clustering. scREFINE uses a lightweight refinement head to map cells into a task-specific clustering space using only 5% labeled cells, while treating the remaining cells as unlabeled during training. To exploit information from unlabeled cells, scREFINE introduces stability-aware soft structural regularization over local neighborhoods, which leverages reliable cell-cell relations as auxiliary guidance without relying on hard pseudo-label constraints. Experiments on five benchmark scRNA-seq datasets show that scREFINE achieves the best ARI on every dataset against every baseline under an identical, leakage-free protocol (mean ± SD over four seeds). A paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test over the five per-dataset means yields p=0.0625, above the conventional 0.05 threshold because only five datasets are available; we therefore interpret the consistent improvements as strong empirical evidence rather than a statistically conclusive demonstration. A common-embedding comparison confirms that these gains arise from task-specific refinement rather than the pretrained representation alone: adapted baselines receiving identical embeddings achieve 0.00-0.61 ARI, compared with 0.73-0.89 for scREFINE. Ablation analyses further demonstrate that task-specific embedding refinement is the primary driver of improvement, whereas soft structural regularization provides dataset-dependent auxiliary gains and degrades more gracefully than hard pseudo-labels when supervision is scarce. Biological marker-gene analysis confirms that the predicted clusters correspond to canonical cell populations.

records.title: Virtual metrology for process perturbation prediction in lithographic alignment marks using a physics-guided directed attention network.
records.abstract: Process perturbations in lithographic alignment marks deform multilayer profiles, break mark symmetry, and introduce alignment position uncertainty. Although alignment position deviation (APD) and wafer quality (WQ) responses contain process-dependent information, retrieving the underlying perturbations remains challenging because the inverse relationship is nonlinear and strongly coupled. We formulate this task as alignment mark virtual metrology, in which process perturbation values are estimated from paired APD/WQ response matrices. To solve this inverse problem, we propose a physics-guided directed attention network (PG-DAN). PG-DAN uses diffraction limit masked attention (DLMA) to inject wavelength, diffraction order, propagation, locality, and identity priors into APD/WQ attention logits, enabling the model to use physically meaningful token relations rather than unconstrained data correlations. A directed decoder further follows multilayer coupling during prediction. Evaluated on a rigorous coupled wave analysis (RCWA) dataset, PG-DAN achieves a mean R2 of 0.999875, a mean range-normalized RMSE of 0.34%, and a mean range-normalized MAE of 0.23%, with lower estimation errors than conventional neural inverse models. These results support physics-guided inverse modeling for alignment mark process perturbation estimation.

records.title: Single-cell perturbation prediction near experimental reproducibility with GENESIS.
records.abstract: Single-cell perturbation atlases now measure cellular responses across millions of cells, but the number of possible combinations of biological contexts, perturbations, doses and other experimental variables make exhaustive measurements infeasible. Here, we present GENESIS (Generative ENErgy-based Single-cell Intervention Simulator), a generative framework that predicts single-cell response distributions directly from the covariates defining an experimental condition. GENESIS uses a lightweight neural network trained with the energy score, a strictly proper scoring rule for distributions. We introduce an experiment-calibrated evaluation framework in which prediction error is interpreted relative to the reproducibility of repeated measurements of the same condition. Across the Tahoe-100M small-molecule atlas and a large PBMC cytokine atlas, GENESIS significantly outperforms existing generative models and statistical baselines and approaches experimental reproducibility on independently repeated conditions. Importantly, GENESIS remains accurate when trained on only a fraction of the available experimental conditions or cells, and generated profiles recover experimentally observed context-dependent transcriptional programs. At comparable training-cell budgets, GENESIS achieves more accurate predictions when measurements span more experimental conditions rather than profiling fewer conditions more deeply. Together, these findings suggest a complementary strategy for perturbation studies: broader, lower-depth measurements can expand experimental coverage, while GENESIS augments sparsely sampled populations and predicts responses in unmeasured conditions.

records.title: MultiFlow: coupled flow matching for predicting single-cell multiomic perturbation responses in unseen cellular contexts.
records.abstract: Predicting cellular responses to perturbation requires resolving coordinated changes across molecular layers, yet most single-cell perturbation models focus on transcriptional responses alone. Here we present MultiFlow, a coupled flow-matching framework that unifies generation and perturbation prediction of paired gene expression and chromatin accessibility. Through bidirectional information exchange between RNA and ATAC generative flows, MultiFlow learns how their joint distribution depends on cellular context and perturbation identity. Across multiomic generation benchmarks, MultiFlow accurately reproduced paired RNA-ATAC states and their population distributions. In multiome perturbation benchmarks, MultiFlow achieved the strongest overall performance in predicting both gene-expression and chromatin-accessibility perturbation responses, outperforming modality-specific perturbation-prediction methods in cell types whose perturbed states were withheld from training. Joint multiomic modeling further preserved perturbation-induced coordination between modalities, including concordant peak-gene effects and cross-modal cellular neighborhood structure. These results establish MultiFlow as a unified generative framework for modeling paired molecular states and predicting their coordinated perturbation responses across cellular contexts. Code and tutorial of MultiFlow are available at https://github.com/liuq-lab/MultiFlow.

records.title: Prediction transfer does not imply reliability transfer in single-cell foundation models.
records.abstract: Single-cell foundation models are increasingly transferred across tissues, diseases, perturbation screens, and experimental platforms. Although substantial effort has focused on prediction transfer, it remains unclear whether a model's assessment of its own reliability transfers similarly across biological contexts. Here we define reliability transfer as the ability to transfer an accurate assessment of when model predictions are likely to be correct or incorrect and investigate its behavior across ten perturbation-prediction systems spanning multiple datasets, models, and evaluation settings. We find that reliability transfer varies substantially across source-target pairs and cannot be inferred from predictive performance alone, indicating that prediction transfer and reliability transfer constitute distinct forms of generalization. Analyses of biological annotations, network connectivity, target exposure, and contextual factors reveal that prediction reliability is associated with both shared and context-dependent signals, with their relative importance differing across systems. To characterize this variability, we introduce reliability-attribution fingerprints, context-level signatures derived from strictly cross-fitted SHAP explanations that summarize how reliability estimators combine biological and contextual information when assigning confidence. Across systems, contexts with similar attribution-magnitude fingerprints tended to transfer reliability more successfully, and fingerprint similarity identified transfer sources achieving higher reliability-transfer performance within the observed candidate set. However, these relationships weakened under stricter cross-family transfer settings, indicating that transferable reliability structure remains partly dependent on shared contextual information. Finally, transferred reliability estimators produced different perturbation rankings despite identical perturbation predictions, illustrating a practical consequence of reliability transfer for downstream prioritization. Together, these results establish reliability transfer as a distinct aspect of foundation-model generalization and introduce reliability-attribution fingerprints as a framework for characterizing transferable reliability structure across biological contexts.

records.title: An AI-designed, recombinantly produced FtsZ-directed peptide with in vitro activity against pan-drug-resistant clinical isolates.
records.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is outpacing the antibiotic pipeline, yet antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) - the most-cited alternative class - remain constrained by proteolytic instability, host toxicity, and the cost of solid-phase synthesis. We report an integrated design-to-validation pipeline that addresses these constraints and yields a de novo peptide directed at an intracellular, non-lytic target. Instead of relying on membrane disruption, the design was directed at FtsZ, the essential bacterial cell-division GTPase, at a consensus epitope (residues 60-145) that our alignments show is substantially more conserved across the Gram-positive/Gram-negative divide than FtsZ overall (68.6% versus 50.1% identity between Enterococcus and Klebsiella orthologues) while sharing only approximately 8-24% identity with human tubulin. A sequence-space diffusion model conditioned on the amino-acid composition of experimentally validated AMPs generated ten binders; fusion to 120 cell-penetrating motifs, machine-learning triage, co-folding and replicated molecular dynamics identified a single lead, Combined111. Rather than chemical synthesis, the peptide was produced biologically: the codon-optimised gene was cloned in-house into pHT254 and expressed as an intracellular, C-terminal 8xHis-tagged product in the protease-deficient Bacillus subtilis WB800N host, giving a mean transcript induction of 3.40-fold (SD 2.01, n = 4 biological replicates) and a single band of approximately 11.1 kDa after one-step Ni-NTA purification. Against one pan-drug-resistant clinical isolate of each of seven species, the purified peptide produced larger inhibition zones than a panel of last-resort antibiotics for five of the seven, by a mean of 4.81 mm, although this difference was not statistically significant (95% CI -0.64 to 10.27; t(6) = 2.16, p = 0.074, Cohen's dz = 0.82). Each zone value is a single measurement, so reproducibility was not assessed, and inhibition-zone diameters are not a direct measure of comparative potency. The advantage was consistent in direction but not uniform, the pan-drug-resistant Enterococcus faecalis isolate being the least susceptible. E. faecium FtsZ was the sequence used for the computational design, whereas the Gram-positive organism available for experimental testing was E. faecalis. These findings show that generative design can be coupled to low-cost bacterial expression in one laboratory. FtsZ-directed inhibition is presented here as a hypothesis rather than an established mechanism: target engagement was inferred from alignment, co-folding and molecular dynamics, and no direct binding measurement, FtsZ polymerisation or GTPase assay, or Z-ring localisation experiment was performed. Minimum inhibitory concentrations, resistance selection, haemolysis, mammalian cytotoxicity, and in vivo efficacy all remain to be established.

records.title: PRIZM: combining low-N data and zero-shot models to design enhanced protein variants.
records.abstract: Machine learning has repeatedly shown the ability to accelerate protein engineering, but many approaches demand large amounts of robust, high-quality training data as well as substantial computational expertise. While large pre-trained models can function as zero-shot proxies for predicting variant effects, selecting the best model for a given protein property is often non-trivial. Here, we introduce Protein Ranking using Informed Zero-shot Modelling (PRIZM), a two-phase workflow that first uses a high-quality low-N dataset to identify the most suitable pre-trained zero-shot model for a target protein property and then applies that model to rank and prioritize an in silico variant library for experimental testing. Across diverse benchmark datasets spanning multiple protein properties, PRIZM reliably separated low- from high-performing models using datasets of ∼20 labelled variants. We further demonstrate PRIZM in enzyme engineering case studies targeting sucrose synthase thermostability and glycosyltransferase activity, where PRIZM-guided selection identified improved variants, including gains of ∼3°C in apparent melting temperature and ∼20% higher relative activity. PRIZM provides an accessible, data-efficient route to leverage foundation models for protein design while requiring minimal experimental data. PRIZM is publicly available via Zenodo, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23035983, and the PRIZM GitHub repository https://github.com/daha-la/PRIZM.

records.title: Tuned Fitness Landscapes for Benchmarking Model-Guided Protein Design.
records.abstract: Machine learning-guided directed evolution (MLDE) is an emerging paradigm of protein design where ML models trained on experimental data are used to guide exploration of a protein fitness landscape. Building an MLDE pipeline involves many design choices across the design-build-test-learn loop ranging from data collection strategies to modeling. The cost of collecting experimental data makes benchmarking every component of these pipelines prohibitively difficult, necessitating the development of synthetic landscapes. In this work, we develop a framework called SLIP ("Synthetic Landscape Inference for Proteins") for constructing synthetic landscapes with tunable difficulty based on Potts models. This framework can be extended to any protein family for which there is a sequence alignment. We show that our tuning framework provides landscapes sufficiently challenging to benchmark MLDE pipelines. SLIP is open-source and is available at https://github.com/google-research/slip.

records.title: AI-Assisted Molecular Structure Prediction from Tandem Mass Spectra: Reliability and Validation.
records.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has broadened the interpretation of tandem mass spectra (MS/MS) beyond experimental library matching, enabling molecular fingerprint prediction, candidate ranking, and generation of previously unlisted structures. Yet these outputs do not all support the same claim about chemical identity. This review briefly summarizes database-restricted retrieval, database-free generation, and scaffold-guided hybrid methods, and then asks what additional evidence is needed to turn a plausible structure into a defensible annotation. We examine failure modes involving incomplete candidate spaces, erroneous precursor assignments, structurally related isomers, leakage between training and test data, and misinterpreted confidence scores. The review contributes two practical elements: a candidate-discrimination workflow, in which alternative structures are retained and targeted measurements such as multienergy fragmentation, retention behavior, ion mobility, and authentic standards are selected according to the unresolved structural question; and an evidence-to-claim checklist that links each question to the most informative measurement and to the strongest supportable identification confidence level. Both synthesize established analytical principles for small-molecule electrospray LC-HRMS/MS rather than constituting a validated scoring algorithm. By making the basis of each annotation transparent, they are intended to improve the practical value of AI-assisted MS/MS in metabolomics, pharmaceutical analysis, environmental screening, and forensic toxicology.

records.title: Emerging Computational Advances in Simulating PCSK9 Variant Dynamics for Therapeutic Design Against Hypercholesterolemia.
records.abstract: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) is a premier model for precision medicine, having moved from genetic discovery to approved therapeutics within two decades. Yet despite the clinical success of monoclonal antibodies, small interfering RNA and the newly approved oral macrocyclic-peptide inhibitor class, targeting PCSK9 remains a demanding biophysical challenge. Clinical translation has concentrated almost entirely on the rigid, well-resolved subtilisin-like catalytic domain that interfaces with the low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR). By contrast, the C-terminal cysteine- and histidine-rich domain (CHRD), which governs allosteric regulation, protein trafficking and post-translational modification, is highly disordered and largely elusive in experimental structures, leaving a critical regulatory network therapeutically unexploited. This review examines how advanced computational biology is bridging that structural gap, organizing the computational landscape of PCSK9 around the biophysical mechanisms of gain- and loss-of-function variants. We detail how explicit-solvent molecular dynamics, free-energy calculations and cryptic-pocket detection expose the functional plasticity and allosteric networks that static crystallography cannot capture, and we evaluate the convergence of these physics-based approaches with artificial intelligence, including deep-learning structure prediction and generative design of de novo nanobody and peptide binders. Therapeutic development and the structural literature currently point in diverging directions: drug discovery remains focused on the crowded LDLR-binding interface, whereas computational methods are beginning to identify candidate sites beyond it. We argue that the next advance in PCSK9 therapeutics will come from integrating generative artificial intelligence with rigorous enhanced sampling in a unified pipeline, deliberately shifting focus toward the disordered regulatory domains that have evaded classical screening.

records.title: A Synthetic Benchmark for Topology-Aware Modeling of Multispecific Antibody Function.
records.abstract: Multispecific antibodies (msAbs) offer transformative therapeutic potential by engaging multiple epitopes simultaneously, yet their efficacy is an emergent property governed by complex molecular architectures. Rational design is often bottlenecked by the inability to predict how subtle changes in domain topology influence functional outcomes, a challenge exacerbated by the scarcity of comprehensive experimental data. Here, we introduce Synapse, a biologically inspired synthetic benchmark for topology-aware modeling of msAbs. First, we present a generative method that combines nonlinear per-domain sequence-to-score landscapes with connectivity-dependent synthetic readouts. Second, we propose a graph neural network architecture that explicitly encodes these topological constraints, distinguishing between format configurations that appear identical to the evaluated connectivity-agnostic multilayer perceptron. We demonstrate that this model learns topology-dependent structure-function relationships on synthetic landscapes and evaluate a transfer learning workflow as infrastructure for adaptation to biological datasets. We showcase our framework with a trispecific T cell engager-inspired synthetic topology-dependent optimization task and a constrained ranking of common light chain candidates against a composite objective. This work provides a controlled benchmarking environment for developing and evaluating topology-aware computational tools for msAb modeling. All experiments use synthetic data; no biological validation is performed.

records.title: Exhaled Breath Condensate-Derived Extracellular Vesicles Isolated via Nanobody-SpyTag3 Fusion Proteins Enable Lung Cancer Diagnosis.
records.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) carry molecular fingerprints of their parent cells, making them attractive liquid biopsy targets. Specific and efficient isolation and retrieval of intact EVs enable comprehensive analysis of EV cargo; however, current approaches remain suboptimal. Here, anti-CD9 nanobody-SpyTag3 fusion proteins were developed to immunoisolate EVs from exhaled breath condensate (EBC) for DNA mutation analysis in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Within 2 h, this assay achieves 94% and 47% EV enrichment from biomimetic EBC and plasma, respectively, outperforming traditional physical methods. Subsequent restriction enzyme treatment recovers 95% of intact EVs within 2 h. Pilot clinical data suggest that EBC EVs may be better suited for early-stage central-type NSCLC, whereas plasma EVs may perform better in advanced peripheral-type cases. In summary, we present a new tool for EV-based diagnosis, highlight the potential of EBC EVs for noninvasive lung cancer detection, and demonstrate the impact of biofluid selection on diagnostic performance.

records.title: Diagnostic threshold optimization of a keratin 17-based urine liquid biopsy assay for urothelial carcinoma detection in patients with hematuria.
records.abstract: To evaluate candidate keratin 17-positive urothelial cell-count thresholds for a urine-based cellular liquid biopsy assay in patients undergoing hematuria evaluation. This retrospective diagnostic accuracy study included 746 voided urine specimens from 612 adults evaluated for microscopic or gross hematuria between August 2019 and March 2026. Urothelial carcinoma-positive outcomes required histopathologic confirmation. Negative classification incorporated cystoscopy, imaging, cytology, urinalysis, and clinical follow-up, as available. Thresholds of ≥5, ≥10, ≥15, and ≥20 keratin 17-positive urothelial cells were compared. Diagnostic performance and continuous cell-count receiver operating characteristic analysis were assessed. Urothelial carcinoma was identified in 23 of 746 specimens. Continuous keratin 17-positive cell counts demonstrated an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.965 (95% confidence interval, 0.949-0.980). At ≥5 cells, sensitivity was 100.0% and specificity was 85.2%. At ≥10 cells, sensitivity was 91.3% and specificity was 92.1%. Increasing the threshold from ≥5 to ≥10 cells reduced false-positive classifications from 107 to 57 while increasing false-negative classifications from 0 to 2. Thresholds of ≥15 and ≥ 20 cells increased specificity to 94.2% and 95.3%, respectively, while reducing sensitivity to 87.0% and 78.3%. Among the evaluated thresholds, ≥10 keratin 17-positive urothelial cells was the highest candidate threshold that maintained sensitivity above 90% while reducing false-positive classifications compared with ≥5 cells. Independent prospective validation is needed before establishing a clinical operating threshold.

records.title: Unlocking Colorectal Cancer Diagnostics With Circulating Progastrin (hPG80): A Scoping Review.
records.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) represents a significant global health concern, ranking as the third most diagnosed cancer and the second leading cause of cancer deaths in the UK. Although population-based bowel cancer screening programs (BCSP) facilitate early diagnosis, uptake remains variable. Blood-based biomarkers, such as human progastrin 80 (hPG80), offer a patient-friendly approach to enhance screening compliance and clinical management. This scoping review, conducted according to PRISMA-ScR guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420250654595), searched Ovid Medline/PubMed, Ovid Embase, and Cochrane databases from January 1990 to January 2025. Studies assessing plasma hPG80 as a CRC biomarker were included, while reviews, in vitro studies, and animal models were excluded. Quality assessment was performed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and findings were synthesized narratively. Five articles encompassing 2,692 participants met the inclusion criteria. The included studies consistently demonstrated significant overexpression of hPG80 in CRC patients compared to non-cancer controls, with an increased median progastrin concentration in the CRC group (27.5 pmol/L) compared to patients with polyps or normal controls. Furthermore, hPG80 levels decreased significantly post-surgery (from 272.3 ± 12.0 pmol/L to 161.3 ± 11.0 pmol/L), reflecting its sensitivity to tumor burden and potential for treatment monitoring. Methodologically, literature has shifted from early radioimmunoassays to safer, cost-effective enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISA). A meta-analysis was not feasible due to variations in analytes, assays, populations, thresholds, and a lack of CRC-specific sensitivity, specificity, or area under the curve data. This review highlights hPG80's promise as a reliable, reproducible blood-based biomarker for CRC integration into BCSPs and symptomatic pathways. However, optimal thresholds, stage-specific correlation, molecular subtypes, and cost-effectiveness remain unanswered. The ongoing MOTION trial (NCT07035691) is currently evaluating hPG80's performance within UK symptomatic suspected colorectal cancer referral pathways.

records.title: Fragment-end sequence architecture of cell-free DNA and its association with tumour DNA in non-small cell lung cancer.
records.abstract: Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragmentation patterns provide a promising source of molecular information for liquid biopsy applications. However, the sequence features underlying fragmentation and their relationship to tumour-derived DNA remain incompletely understood. Here, we characterized fragment-end sequence signatures of extracellular cfDNA across cell lines, extracellular compartments, stress conditions and plasma from patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). cfDNA derived from cell lines was characterized using Oxford Nanopore sequencing, followed by fragment-end analysis. Publicly available Nanopore cfDNA datasets from healthy individuals and NSCLC patients were analyzed to examine dinucleotide patterns and derive a motif ratio index. These signatures were further assessed for their association with estimated ctDNA abundance in an independent cohort of 50 EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients. Nanopore sequencing of A549, H460 and WI38 cell-line cfDNA revealed reproducible end-motif patterns, with enrichment of AT-, GT- and CT-containing termini. Analysis of plasma cfDNA from healthy individuals showed distinct end-motif profiles from cell-line-derived cfDNA, with separation maintained after reducing 4-mer motifs to 5'-terminal dinucleotide features. An exploratory motif ratio based on these patterns showed a modest increase in lung cancer patients compared with healthy individuals. In an independent Illumina cohort of 50 NSCLC patients with activating EGFR mutations, 5'-terminal dinucleotide frequencies were associated with estimated circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) abundance using cross-validated LASSO (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator) regression (Spearman ρ = .73, p = 3.35 × 10‒9). The predefined motif ratio showed a strong correlation with estimated ctDNA concentration (Spearman ρ = .76, p = 1.89 × 10‒10). These findings suggest that simple, interpretable cfDNA end-motif signatures capture sequence features associated with ctDNA abundance and warrant further validation for non-invasive cancer monitoring.

records.title: Machine Learning-Driven ZnO NRs@Ag SERS Platform for Rheumatoid Arthritis Liquid Biopsy in a Multicenter-Recruited Cohort.
records.abstract: The analytical chemistry diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) faces challenges such as the time lag of conventional serological assays and matrix masking in complex biofluid analysis. This study proposes a label-free liquid biopsy framework integrating band-regulated surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) sensing with machine learning algorithms. Experimental characterizations (XPS and TRPL) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm that the ZnO NRs@Ag heterojunction drives efficient spatial separation of charge carriers via stepped band alignment. This achieves a deep synergy between electromagnetic (EM) and chemical enhancements (CM), significantly improving the signal selectivity of metabolites against high-abundance backgrounds. Meanwhile, the substrate exhibits good batch-to-batch structural reproducibility and environmental storage stability. Based on this sensing platform, a patient-level internal validation was conducted on a multicenter-recruited serum cohort. By averaging replicate spectra to prevent data leakage, the model classification was strictly performed on 74 independent patient-level input features (comprising 66 RA cases and 8 healthy controls). Under a leave-one-patient-out cross-validation architecture coupled with dynamic in-fold oversampling, the linear classification model (PLS-DA) achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.9337. Furthermore, utilizing the SHAP method, the model identified putative spectral features that influenced the classification decision, providing a reference for exploring related pathological metabolic changes. This study elucidates the synergistic enhancement mechanism of the heterojunction at the electronic state level and verifies the preliminary diagnostic potential of the platform in decoding high-dimensional metabolic profiles, offering a methodological foundation for applying SERS technology to autoimmune disease screening.

records.title: Time-Resolved Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy Profiling of Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells Reveals Convergent Immunosuppressive Remodeling in Glioblastoma.
records.abstract: Systemic immune dysfunction is a hallmark of glioblastoma (GBM) progression and therapeutic resistance, yet rapid, minimally invasive methods for sensing dynamic immune-cell state changes remain limited. Here, we introduce a label-free surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) immune-sensing framework that uses peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) biochemical profiles as an accessible readout of GBM-associated systemic immunosuppression. Ag nanoparticle-decorated black silicon SERS substrates were used to profile PBMCs in GBM-PBMC coculture models representing early and progressed tumor-immune interaction states over 3-72 h. Multivariate spectral analysis, correlation-network mapping, pseudotime analysis, partial least-squares regression, and transfer learning were then used to define Raman-detected immune remodeling. SERS detected GBM-induced PBMC biochemical divergence within 3 h and resolved distinct intermediate remodeling trajectories that converged by 72 h into a shared immunosuppressive signature separated from astrocyte-interacted controls. Partial least-squares regression organized the PBMC spectra into a time-associated immunosuppression trajectory with strong predictive performance (R2 = 0.84). These results were corroborated by flow cytometry, which demonstrated reduced T-cell activation and time-dependent myeloid remodeling over the co-culture period. A ResNet-1D model trained only on the in vitro SERS dataset classified 6 independent GBM patient buffy coat samples as GBM-like with >99.9% confidence, and similarity analysis showed close correspondence between patient spectra and GBM-conditioned PBMC signatures. These results establish SERS-based immune-cell profiling as a label-free strategy for sensing and modeling GBM-associated systemic immune remodeling and support its further development for minimally invasive liquid-biopsy applications.
